22.label: Beadle Pietersz
22.desc: A parish beadle with a staff and a loud voice. Knocks on doors without complaining and whips beggars without being asked. Slot them into a verb to help. Thorough: Finds one more thing at every scene.

38.label: Burglary at the Bakker House
38.desc: Bartel Cooper is not sure when it happened: some time between Friday night and Monday morning. Only the study casement was touched, and only the strongbox, opened rather than forced taken. A neighbour reports seeing a guest who left early. Somebody knew the house. (The Market) The Bishop asks mercy for whoever did this, if they repent: a Pardon or a Fine, not the rope.

42.label: The Scene Drawn
42.desc: Forty leaves of the Bakker House in charcoal, numbered and dated. The room as it was.

44.label: The Inventory
44.desc: What the house says was taken does not match the guild's inventory. Someone knew what was worth carrying.

45.label: Ned Vos
45.desc: Ned Vos, a receiver from the Market. Has lately paid a carrier for a seat on the wagon to the coast. (Accused in: Burglary at the Bakker House)

48.label: Old Offender: Cicely Tanner
48.desc: Old Offender, crocheteur. 2 crimes on the record. Walks with a heavy limp in the left leg. Has stood before the Blood Court once. Leaves less behind.

51.label: Protection in the Welser Arcade
51.desc: Stallholders have been paying for "protection" for months. Now Moll Fuller's stall has had its awning slashed and its stock in the gutter for refusing. Nobody else will talk. (The Market)

52.label: Partial: The Blade Read
52.desc: Without a Physician's Case, you only get part of it. The blade was a chisel, chipped at one corner. Find the chisel, find the burglar.

55.label: Pipe Ash on the Sill
55.desc: A knocked-out bowl of ash on the windowsill, still sour. Someone waited here a long while, smoking.

57.label: Ned Hobson
57.desc: Ned Hobson, a nephew of the house. Smokes a clay pipe of cheap Dutch tobacco, one bowl after another. (Accused in: Burglary at the Bakker House)

59.label: Partial: The Tobacco Named
59.desc: Without a Physician's Case, you only get part of it. Cheap leaf, sold at two shops in the city. Both keep a slate for regulars.

62.label: The Second Key
62.desc: The strongbox was opened, not forced. Three people have a key. One of them lent it.

63.label: Moll de Witt
63.desc: Moll de Witt, the night porter. Left-handed. Writes with a hooked wrist. (Accused in: Burglary at the Bakker House)

journal.title: A Room at the Swan
journal.text: The landlord of the Swan, who owes the Watch a kindness, offers a room with a fire and a door that locks. One night. Tonight. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: Week 6
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 1. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. Out there, the people who walked are talking about you. The Provost has sent an examiner of his own. The ledger: no case closed; 2 open; 11 Coin in hand.

journal.title: The Provost's Examiner
journal.text: Margarethe Sturm has the Provost's letter and a desk on the other side of the Market. They will work your cases from the other side: close them first, spoil your scenes, pay your witnesses to forget. Question them, buy them, frighten them, or shadow them; find their weakness twice and the Council sends them home.

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: You go back over the Bakker House. You find: The Second Key. A neighbour, leaning on the gate, offers a name: Moll de Witt. The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: Entered
journal.text: Four hours with the quill. By the end, even the parts that were not quite by the Carolina read as if they were.

journal.title: Partial Results
journal.text: Without a Physician's Case, you only get part of it. Cheap leaf, sold at two shops in the city. Both keep a slate for regulars. You worked into the dark, and it cost you.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: Week 5
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 1. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. Out there, the people who walked are talking about you. Cicely Tanner has done it again: Protection in the Welser Arcade. The ledger: 1 acquittal; 2 open; 10 Coin in hand.

journal.title: Cicely Tanner Again
journal.text: The hand is familiar. Stallholders have been paying for "protection" for months. Now Moll Fuller's stall has had its awning slashed and its stock in the gutter for refusing. Nobody else will talk.

journal.title: Not Guilty: Cicely Tanner
journal.text: The sworn men acquit. Cicely Tanner walks down the court steps into the crowd's cheering and looks straight at you.

journal.title: At the Scene
journal.text: You go in past the beadle at the Bakker House. The back shutter has been forced with something flat and patient, and the strongbox stands open like a mouth. You come away with The Pried Shutter, The Inventory. A name for the board: Ned Vos. The back room stayed locked, and the hard way in wore you out.

journal.title: Taken: Cicely Tanner
journal.text: The sergeants take them at the city gate, one foot on the carrier's wagon. The charge is full proof. Now it is for the sworn men.

journal.title: Hands and Hours
journal.text: What was left behind, and who could have been there to leave it. The marks narrow the door until only one person fits through it. It was Cicely Tanner, the night porter. It has to be.

journal.title: Cleared: Bess Nagel
journal.text: You try Bess Nagel's story. It holds: a night in the Hole for drunkenness. Scratch one name off the board.

journal.title: Nothing Doing
journal.text: The city is quiet tonight. It is never quiet for long. The long way round, and your legs know it.

journal.title: Pocketed
journal.text: Three weeks' stipend in worn silver. It sits in your coat like a stone. Somewhere, somebody writes your name in a ledger.

journal.title: A Round Walked
journal.text: Veit Pietersz walks the round without complaint. The Council's ledger reads your name.

journal.title: The Desk Under the Stair
journal.text: The desk is yours now: the tallow stub, the cracked inkhorn, the case already waiting on it. The last examiner to sit here left in a hurry. The city did not stop to notice.

journal.title: New Case: Burglary at Welser's Pawnshop
journal.text: Glass everywhere at Stoffel Chandler's. Someone went through the shutter, with a crow at the dead of the night, took whatever was in the till, and was gone before the watchman finished shouting. A neighbour reports seeing somebody laughing.

choice.title: A Room at the Swan

options.label: Take the room
options.text: You sleep like the dead and wake like the living.

options.label: Work through
options.text: A Coin for the night's writing, and the ache goes a little deeper.
